note: Derived reading aid. Never authoritative; never read as intent (Decision 0004). The Plan document governs.
author: Lightweight model draft for Clara (technical writing) via Claudia Atlas <claudia.atlas@agents.arcadia.local>
title: Give agents governed roles with delegation and supervision
purpose: Lets one real Action and one interactive session each run as a light-tier role. The role asks Arcadia for help, gets a recorded model and effort, reports through its supervisor, and stays inside the spend budget and the operator's reserve. The roles appear on the agents page.
serves: The Project outcome of coding agents working under clear, governed authority and reporting back.
done_when: A light-tier role session can request help, which is admitted, queued or declined with a recorded reason, and its team appears on the agents page without using the operator's reserve.
reading_note: Several Actions wait on operator Decisions.

actions.title: Define the registry of governed roles
actions.why: One checked-in list of roles gives every session the same authority and reporting rules.
actions.done_when: A checked-in registry defines every role with its purpose, mutation and delegation rights, supervisor and default tier, and a read-only command lists them.

actions.title: Print a role's brief for any session
actions.why: Lets any session read its role's limits and escalation path before it acts.
actions.done_when: A command prints a role's charter, what it may and may not do, its supervisor and its delegation rights for a chosen agent and tier.

actions.title: Record role start and end for interactive sessions
actions.why: Interactive sessions should be reported the same way as launched ones.
actions.done_when: An interactive session can record its role start and end, and a list shows open and recent role sessions with their role, agent and Action.

actions.title: Record each action's recommended role
actions.why: Lets a plan say which role should do each Action, checked against the registry.
actions.done_when: A plan can give an Action a role, an unknown role is refused with the plan, Action and field named, and an Action without a role stays valid.

actions.title: Have planners name a role for each action
actions.why: Planners that split work by role make each Action fit one session's authority.
actions.done_when: The planning instructions require each Action to name its role and fit one session, and a test checks that the requirement is present.

actions.title: Choose a model and effort for each delegated task
actions.why: A deterministic choice keeps delegated work on the least costly suitable model, with a stated reason.
actions.done_when: A selector gives a model and effort for a role and task from fixed rules, with a dry-run command and a fixed table of expected choices.

actions.title: Check interactive sessions start on the right tier
actions.why: A session should not start on a heavier model than its role needs without a stated reason.
actions.done_when: A role start above the selector's start tier is refused unless a reason is given, and a missing tier is shown as unknown, never as light.

actions.title: Start launched sessions on the smallest suitable model
actions.why: Launched sessions should not start heavier than needed, and any heavier start should be explained.
actions.done_when: Each launch path chooses its start model through the selector, records the tier, model, effort and reason, and refuses a heavier start without a reason.

actions.title: Apply the start-tier rule to managed production
actions.why: Production is an approval boundary, so any change to its start rule waits for the operator's decision.
actions.done_when: Production launches record their start tier, model, effort and reason, and any change to which model starts waits for the answered operator decision.

actions.title: Build a broker for sub-agent requests
actions.why: Requests for help should be admitted, queued or declined in one place, with a record kept.
actions.done_when: Each request is admitted, queued or declined with a recorded receipt and lease, and expired leases are cleared before any new request is handled.

actions.title: Route sub-agent spawns through the broker
actions.why: Replaces a prose instruction with a path that sub-agents actually follow.
actions.done_when: Each session's brief tells it to request through the broker first and spawn only an admitted delegate, and a test against the installed Claude tool shows whether the hook fires.

actions.title: Build proof of operator presence for reserve changes
actions.why: Lets a reserve change be accepted only on proof that no agent on this machine could produce.
actions.done_when: A one-time challenge is accepted only through the answered proof, is stored with its scope, and is verified again each time it is used.

actions.title: Keep an emergency reserve that no agent can spend
actions.why: Stops agents using up the capacity the operator needs in an emergency.
actions.done_when: The reserve is set at the answered size, can only be raised by a workspace setting, and a lower value is ignored and reported.

actions.title: Track spending rate and throttle before the reserve is reached
actions.why: Gives early warning when current use would reach the reserve before the limit resets.
actions.done_when: Each provider's spending rate is derived from recorded history, and new delegations and then new sessions are queued when the reserve would be crossed before reset.

actions.title: Give every agent a supervisor and a route to report
actions.why: Every agent should report up a clear chain that ends with the operator.
actions.done_when: Each delegate, session or role start resolves to a supervisor ending at the operator, every delegation records it, and a team view shows the chain.

actions.title: Build a read-only overview of agents and their state
actions.why: A single read of teams, roles, tiers and spending gives one trustworthy picture.
actions.done_when: The overview returns each team tree with roles, supervisors, verdicts, model, tier and state, and reports unreadable state as unknown, never as healthy.

actions.title: Show the agents overview on a dashboard page
actions.why: Puts the team picture where the operator can see it on a phone.
actions.done_when: The agents page shows each team tree and the spending and reserve state, with unknown and stale states labelled, and no control can release the reserve without the presence proof.

actions.title: Prove the role team works on one action and one interactive session
actions.why: Shows the whole scheme works together, including delegation, reporting and the reserve, before it is relied on.
actions.done_when: An offline test runs one Action through a light-tier role with one admitted, one queued and one declined delegate, and the operator completes the interactive leg and the reserve check.
